summary: This script analyzes tags from a collection of articles to find the most frequently used tags and suggest which articles should link to each other based on shared tags. It reads article data from a JSON file, counts tag frequencies, saves the results, and then creates a map of which articles could cross-link based on having common tags.

explanations.9: This gets the parent directory of the parent directory of the current file, so if this script is in project/scripts/, BASE_DIR points to project/.
explanations.19: This flattens a nested structure—it loops through each article and extracts all tags, creating one long list of every tag from every article.
explanations.25: Counter is like a specialized dictionary that counts how many times each tag appears. It's from the collections module and makes the next step easier.
explanations.26: most_common() returns the tags ranked by frequency; we only take the top 20 (defined by TOP_TAGS_COUNT).
explanations.35: This builds a list of dictionaries by looping through the most common tags and formatting each one with its tag name and count.
explanations.54: tag_to_articles is being built as an inverted index—instead of articles pointing to tags, tags point to articles, which makes lookups faster later.
explanations.64: suggested_links is a set so that if two articles share multiple tags, we don't accidentally list the same article twice.
explanations.68: The .get(tag, []) safely retrieves articles for this tag, returning an empty list if the tag somehow isn't in the dictionary.
explanations.75: We convert the set to a sorted list so the output is deterministic and easier to read—sets don't have a guaranteed order.
